what: Supplier swatch-chart catalogue: the species/cut/finish taxonomy and every colour name, transcribed from photographed sample charts.
whyItExists: The app measures a hide's colour but has no name for it. These are the names the operator and Magna actually use ('reads closest to Cognac'). The charts also carry a far richer taxonomy than the app models today -- see taxonomyGaps.
status: PARTIAL -- more charts still being added. 39 chart sections, 413 swatches so far, plus a non-leather section for stitching.
caveats: Colour NAMES only. No measured LAB values yet -- the source images are not in this repo, see sourceImages.
Transcribed by reading the chart photos. Worth spot-checking against the originals before anything depends on exact spelling.

Spelling is recorded as printed, not normalised, and the catalogue contradicts itself in at least four places: 'Terracota' (Italian Pebble 1) vs 'Terra Cota' (Italian Pebble 2) -- same colour, same product line, two spellings; 'Fuschia' (Anaconda) vs 'Fuchsia' (Italian Pebble 2); 'Rosewood' (Italian Pebble 1) vs 'Rose Wood' (Alligator Glazed 2); 'Turqoise' (Ostrich Leg Glossy) vs 'Turquoise' (Alligator Glazed 1). Which spelling is canonical is the supplier's call, not ours, but any name-matching has to survive these.

NOT ALL OF THIS IS EXOTIC. Italian Calf is a plain bovine hide, and Pebble, Suede and Nappa name a grain, a surface and a tannage respectively -- none of them a species, and none of those charts states one. Recorded as species: null rather than guessed at.

FINISH IS SOMETIMES INSIDE THE COLOUR NAME, not the chart heading. Shark lists 'Brown' and 'Brown Suede' side by side on one chart; Lizard 2 has 'Matte Black' and 'Matte Pewter'; Python Glossy has 'Silver Metallic' and 'Gold Metallic'; Ostrich Leg Suede has 'Matte Black'. So the same dye can appear under two unrelated-looking names, and a colour vocabulary built on these strings alone would treat 'Brown' and 'Brown Suede' as different colours. Splitting them needs the supplier's confirmation, not a regex.
Fields are null where the chart does not state them. The alligator glossy/matte/suede charts name no cut; belly is the likely default but the charts do not say so, and guessing is not recording.

'NATURAL' IS NOT A COLOUR, it is the absence of dye -- the animal's own markings. It appears across cobra, radiated snake, viper, flower snake, western diamond rattlesnake and banded water snake, and a Natural cobra looks nothing like a Natural viper. So the SAME colour name means different actual colours depending on species, which any lookup built on these names has to account for.

NOT usable for scale matching: the charts carry no scale reference, so pixels cannot be converted to millimetres. One number would fix that -- the real physical size of a swatch patch on the sample card.

Glossy charts have heavy specular blowout on the saturated colours (Royal Blue, Orange, Yellow, Turquoise). Blown pixels lose chroma, so anything sampled off those will read desaturated. Matte and suede are much cleaner.

sourceImages.note: The chart photos arrived as chat attachments and could not be written to disk from there. To measure LAB per swatch, save the originals into docs/reference/swatches/ and they can be sampled from there.

taxonomyGaps.note: The app models a hide as species + finish, where finish is glossy/matte/semi-gloss. These charts show that is wrong in four ways.
taxonomyGaps.cutIsNotFinish: Hornback, belly, tail, leg and full quill are CUTS -- different parts of the animal, with different scale geometry. Hornback is the back ridge with raised scutes; ostrich leg is scaled like a reptile while ostrich full quill is the bumpy follicle body. Two hides could both be 'alligator, cognac' and never pair because one is hornback. Cut belongs in the model, and it matters for scale matching specifically.
taxonomyGaps.treatmentIsNotFinish: Suede is the flesh side; hand-painted is a surface treatment, sometimes two-tone. Neither is a gloss level.
taxonomyGaps.gradeExists: 'Gnarly' is a grade -- large skins with scars and natural marks, sold deliberately for a rustic look.
taxonomyGaps.originExists: Argentine, American, Australian all appear as qualifiers and plausibly track real differences in the skin.
taxonomyGaps.semiGlossUnconfirmed: 'Semi-gloss' appears in the app but in none of the supplier's charts. Possibly invented on our side.

charts.gradeNote: Cut from very large skins that have scars and natural marks; no holes or open cuts are used. For a more rustic or rugged look.

charts.finishNote: One chart, two finishes: the first ten carry no finish, the last six name suede in the colour itself.
'Matte Black' and 'Matte Pewter' carry the finish in the colour name. 'Ring-marked Natural' is a natural marking, not a dye.
'Silver Metallic' and 'Gold Metallic' name a finish the chart heading does not.

nonLeatherOptions.note: Deliberately NOT in the charts array. These are product construction options, not hide materials -- mixing thread colours into a leather colour vocabulary would corrupt it.
